item.title: Damaging coastal storm conditions have become twice as frequent at a New Jersey Beach since 1979
item.description:
Waypoint is curating and commenting on third-party reporting. Original publisher: Phys.org.
Summary: Storm conditions capable of causing major coastal erosion at New Jersey's North Beach on Sandy Hook are occurring about twice as often as they did in 1979, according to Rutgers researchers. The finding offers new evidence that storm impacts are becoming more frequent along the Mid-Atlantic coast.
Waypoint’s Take: For someone heading outside in the Northeast, the useful question is observational: use the report as a planning signal — precipitation, wind, and visibility change what is safe and worth noticing. item.title: Long-term study suggests landfill methane emissions are far higher than estimates
item.description:
